## Design

### 2026-10-05 – I started by making the schematic and wiring everything together all the connections, the nets, everything joined up in one logical diagram.![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-

**2h**

I started by making the schematic and wiring everything together all the connections, the nets, everything joined up in one logical diagram.![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/b1080c3d4263d4bb631a58a61f3892b996c3070be107c165307f9fd2d2fa075f.png)
the PCB. I took all those footprints and placed them physically, got them arranged where I wanted, and then routed the traces to match the connections I'd already defined. Finally I double checked that everything was placed and routed correctly before calling it done.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/8f01484ebcf66518ea3f4d92cc69047e91d01c501d920c14e01c7bb081e874c0.png)And on top of all that, I'm also thinking about making it portable. adding a battery so I can take it around without plugging in. That's the part I'm still figuring out, but that's the direction I want to go.

### 2026-10-07 – ![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/c7f07918092678cf47001bec62d2a7f5890d940aef7574b7f7a19e6aa27b453f.png)Today the project took a

**2h**

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/c7f07918092678cf47001bec62d2a7f5890d940aef7574b7f7a19e6aa27b453f.png)Today the project took a complete turn, and for a good reason: I realized I didn't want an accessory, I wanted a pet. Something you wear, that has a little face, that reacts to you. So Clicky went from being "a weird keyboard" to being a small heart that lives with you.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/52cca9e624486f776a8dbad3354661a6c783aefdd70ce14c69cf2f52bef82661.png)

### 2026-10-08 – ![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/c94f87ce7c40fe8d478a1077cbad1b3a1337a8ca236b3cc402fa9d9fd01c6e91.png)So I've been drawing thi

**2h**

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/c94f87ce7c40fe8d478a1077cbad1b3a1337a8ca236b3cc402fa9d9fd01c6e91.png)So I've been drawing this schematic in KiCad, and honestly it's going a lot better than I expected. I got the little ESP32-C3 brain in, the motion sensor, the temperature one, the resistor, the pet button, and the battery hookup. And I figured out the net-label thing — calling wires the same name connects them, which is way cleaner than a mess of crossing lines. So 3V3, ground, the I2C lines, the temp wire, the touch button, and the battery are all in.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/334e0d67a12bb1756351e98045bfeda37aba33e47e76bb1b747070ed7255a753.png)But then I hit a wall, the round screen (GC9A01) and the mic just don't show up when I search for them. Turns out they're not in any library because you buy them as little modules already made. The fix is to draw them as generic connectors or just make my own symbol

### 2026-10-09 – ![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/93645fe2ed46b78dd939d850123490279e66d1ee6c72e73d9fdbc1a0db21fa14.png)

**1h**

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/93645fe2ed46b78dd939d850123490279e66d1ee6c72e73d9fdbc1a0db21fa14.png)
Today I kept working on the KiCad schematic for Clicky. A lot of small steps, but they added up: I ran KiCad's ERC over and over to find problems, and I fixed them one by one.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/78f4616c0c9841700b754de46b1739912f2b8fb5bf96bc36a5404a3738a1fbf4.png)I also learned the hard way that a few components had wrong footprints: KiCad was matching a radio connector to the battery, a lever switch to the touch button, and the XIAO's footprint wasn't even being found because I'd given the library the wrong name. I fixed the library name and the footprint now resolves.
